retrieval.method: targeted web search followed by public arXiv HTML retrieval and bounded passage reads
retrieval.note: Response IDs are session retrieval references, not portable evidence; URLs and verbatim excerpts below are portable. Only targeted sections were reviewed, not an exhaustive paper audit. No model assets were fetched.

sources.title: Large Language Models Are Not Robust Multiple Choice Selectors
sources.version_note: Version-specific arXiv HTML is the source of quoted passages. Search also returned the earlier v1 title; v1 was not used as the reviewed text.

passages.quote: One challenge here is that option IDs are bound with options’ ordering positions, e.g., the ID B is naturally tied with the second-presented option.
passages.supports: Default ordinal letters confound label identity and displayed position.
passages.limits: Does not identify which mechanism explains this project's Qwen outputs.

passages.section: 2.4 What Causes Selection Bias?; ID-shuffling ablation
passages.quote: But this ablation will obviously impair the naturalness and quality of the MCQ prompt, and may consequently degrade model performance
passages.supports: Changing label assignment also changes prompt familiarity; do not interpret reversed alphabet prompts as a pure mechanistic intervention.
passages.limits: The paper studied shuffled IDs; the exact descending-letter intervention is our proposed diagnostic, not their measured result.

passages.quote: ensures one pairing between each option ID
passages.supports: Their cyclic design covers every ID/content pairing; reversal alone does not.
passages.limits: This short exact phrase is part of the cyclic-permutation discussion. The formal construction and equation (1), not the excerpt alone, establish the coverage. It does not establish invariance or correction validity for R6.

passages.quote: For tractable derivation, we reasonably assume that
passages.supports: The decomposition relies on assumptions, including invariance of the debiased content distribution to option order and prior independence of the option permutation.
passages.limits: The formal assumptions are in the surrounding paragraph and equation (3). This source permits a question-dependent prior; R6's cross-case fixed b is a stronger additional assumption.

passages.quote: due to the natural binding between option IDs and options’ ordering positions
passages.supports: The source's prior combines token and position bias rather than separately identifying them.
passages.limits: Does not prove either component is static in the proposed packet.

not_used_for: a calibrated or corrected probability claim

sources.title: Leveraging Large Language Models for Multiple Choice Question Answering
sources.version_note: ICLR 2023 paper; the arXiv identifier begins in 2022. Version-specific HTML supplied the reviewed passages.

passages.quote: The probabilities of these symbols therefore serve as a proxy for each answer’s probability.
passages.supports: Symbol-token scoring differs from option-text likelihood scoring.
passages.limits: Proxy answer scores are not established calibrated correctness, and normalized symbol probabilities do not determine full-vocabulary valid-letter mass. The latter is our algebraic observation.

passages.section: 4 The Challenge of Multiple Choice Symbol Binding
passages.quote: Importantly, PPA measures order invariance irrespective of model ability to perform a task. If a model performs poorly on a task but answers consistently across possible orders of answer options it will still have a high PPA.
passages.supports: Consistency/order invariance is distinct from task accuracy; descriptive contrast fidelity should not be sold as correctness.
passages.limits: Their PPA uses all permutations; R6's two/four-cell contrast diagnostic is not exhaustive-permutation PPA.

original_analysis_not_source_claims: Centered paired log ratios identify gamma_j=b_j-b_mirror under invariant per-case content utility.
Mirror-symmetric bias changes can be absorbed into case-specific utilities; antisymmetric b is gamma/2.
The four-cell letter mapping and alpha/beta contrasts, residual sign pattern and residual identifiability limits.
One source-held-out constrained descriptive fit, hierarchical source/group/case/option weights, fidelity summaries and zero-handling protocol.
Conditional option probabilities cannot recover full-vocabulary valid-letter probability mass.
No accuracy, correction, calibration or exclusive causal inference follows from descriptive fit.
